item.title: 5 Types of SQL Database Commands Every Developer Should Know
item.description: Understanding and mastering SQL database commands is crucial for developers working with relational databases. This article explores five fundamental types of SQL commands that every developer should be familiar with. These commands cover various aspects of database management, including data retrieval, manipulation, and schema management. 1. SELECT - Retrieving Data: The SELECT statement is fundamental for retrieving data from one or more tables. It allows developers to specify the columns they want to retrieve, apply filtering conditions, and sort the results.

item.title: MySQL DISTINCT Clause - VS Code
item.description: Introduction to MySQL DISTINCT Clause When querying data from a table, duplicate rows may be retrieved. To remove these duplicates, the DISTINCT clause is used in the SELECT statement. The syntax for the DISTINCT clause is as follows: SELECT DISTINCT select_list FROM table_name WHERE search_condition ORDER BY sort_expression; In this syntax, you specify one or more columns in the select_list to obtain distinct values. If one column is specified, uniqueness is evaluated based on its values.

item.title: MySQL AND Operator - VS Code
item.description: Introduction to MySQL AND Operator MySQL uses the number zero for FALSE and non-zero values for TRUE, as it doesn’t have a built-in Boolean type. The AND operator is a logical operator that combines two or more Boolean expressions and returns 1, 0, or NULL. item.title: MySQL IN Operator - VS Code
item.description: The MySQL IN Operator for Efficient Queries In the vast landscape of database management, MySQL stands out as a powerful and versatile choice. One of the key features that contribute to its flexibility is the IN operator, a valuable tool for simplifying and optimizing queries. In this tutorial, we’ll delve into the intricacies of the MySQL IN operator and explore its applications. The IN operator allows you to check if a value matches any value in a specified list.
